text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A 600,000 Ecu credit line extended to Bulgaria under EU's PHARE programme to support small private businesses in 1996 has not been used, a representative for a local business grouping said.

-- Bulgarians have transfered some $250 million to $300 million abroad in the first half of 1996 because of the istability of the country's banking system, the semi-annual report of the central bank said.
-- Bulgaria's gross domestic product fell 8.2 percent in the second quater of 1996 compared to the same period of 1995, the National Statistics Institute said.

-- The Russian private corporation NITEK is interested in the privatisation of the Bulgaria's drug maker Sopharma, NITEK's vice president Viktor Taknov said after talks with Privatisation Agency's director Vesselin Blagoev.
Bulgaria was the only ex-communist country to offer attractive privatisation deals for NITEK, added Taknov.

-- Bulgaria's cabinet is ready to report some progress in the on-going economic reforms to the International Monetary Fund as 64 loss making companies were closed down and the first voucher privatisation tender is to be completed by the end of October, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- Central bank foreign currency refinancing to local commercial banks totalled some $160 million in the first six months of 1996, the central bank said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
